deleted.reason: No exhaustive end-to-end zero-cost basket count; bulk billing does not measure zero production cost.
Human-required versus automatable baskets and weights remain unjustified.
Service cost barriers do not measure household resources minus a local living basket.
NERO nowcasts are not linked displaced-worker recovery durations.
Spatial GP FTE distribution does not measure corporate ownership or productive-power control.
Health literacy and GP waits do not measure social-protection delivery readiness.
Patient experience cannot stand in for repeated technology-transition consent.
One-country basket does not measure cross-border eligibility differences.

added.justification: Retained because reported cost-related delay or non-use observes a price barrier to the GP pathway, including people who needed care but did not obtain it. It adds an access outcome that a fee schedule alone cannot show. The annual NSW survey estimate is not household affordability, an individual diagnosis or evidence that price dominates other barriers.
added.population: Usual residents aged 15 years and over in private dwellings, within the survey scope, who needed the specified service in the preceding 12 months
added.owner: General practices set fees and bulk-billing choices; Australian Government sets Medicare benefits

added.justification: Retained as a separate administrative view of the payment condition among patients with Medicare GP attendances. It tests whether a patient incurred any GP gap over the year, complementing rather than replicating self-reported cost delay. People with no claimed attendance are absent, so a rising share cannot establish access among non-users.
added.population: Patients with Medicare GP non-referred attendances in the year
added.owner: General practices set fees and bulk-billing choices; Australian Government sets Medicare benefits

added.justification: Retained because obtaining a consultation does not establish access to the prescribed medicine. Reported prescription delay or non-use due to cost measures a distinct downstream price barrier among survey-scope people needing medicines. The aggregate covers prescriptions generally, not atorvastatin-specific availability or adherence.
added.population: Usual residents aged 15 years and over in private dwellings, within the survey scope, who needed the specified service in the preceding 12 months

added.justification: Retained to test timeliness alongside the price indicators, so lower cost is not treated as sufficient access. It measures the reported wait of urgent GP users, with published uncertainty, rather than inferring capacity from workforce totals. Unmet urgent need is excluded; four hours is a reported time category, not a universal clinical standard.
added.population: Survey-scope residents aged 15 years and over who saw a GP for urgent medical care
added.owner: General practices and PHNs, with government workforce and service funding
